READING-SLOWLY(1)               User Commands                READING-SLOWLY(1)

NAME
       Reading slowly

DESCRIPTION
       Why a page read twice is read once.

       reading · terminals

       A page read twice is read once, if the first reading was slow.[1]

WHAT A READER KEEPS
       Reading  Kept
       ───────  ──────
       Fast     Little
       Slow     Most

       - the margins
       - the notes
         - in pencil[2]
         - in ink

       │ A book is read with a pencil.
       │
       │ Twice, with a pen.

       A noted margin
       <https://example.test/blog/reading-slowly/margin.png>
       The margin, where a slow reader writes back.

       In a terminal
              3. open the file
              4. read it with less

              // slowly reads a page twice, aloud
              func slowly(page string) int {
                  fmt.Println("slowly", page)
                  return len(page) * 2
              }

              less "$HOME/notes"

              See the reader's notes, or write to mira@example.test.[1]

AFTERWARDS
       A page kept is a page read again, as what a reader keeps
       <https://example.test/blog/reading-slowly.txt> says, and the tool
       <https://example.test/p/tidy-tool.txt> that tidies it.


                                      *   *   *


       What stays is what was argued with.

NOTES
       [1] Mira Example, on her own reading.
       [2] A soft one, which rubs out.
